implemented_requirements.requirement: Movement only on floor tiles, cannot pass through walls
implemented_requirements.evidence: move() checks "if not (0 <= nx < GRID and 0 <= ny < GRID) or self.grid[ny][nx]: return" where self.grid[y][x]==1 denotes a wall

implemented_requirements.requirement: Goal is to reach the door to proceed to the next level
implemented_requirements.evidence: self.door = (n - 3, n - 3) and in move(): "if (nx, ny) == self.door and not self.dead: self.level += 1; self.build_level()"

implemented_requirements.requirement: Monsters encountered; combat subtracts monster HP from player HP
implemented_requirements.evidence: When a monster entity is stepped on: "self.hp -= mhp" where mhp is the monster's HP

implemented_requirements.requirement: HP restored by 20–30 points when the player touches a treasure chest
There is always at least one valid path from the starting position to the door
implemented_requirements.evidence: build_level() creates a perfect maze using a depth‑first stack algorithm guaranteeing connectivity of all carved cells, including the door at (n‑3, n‑3)

implemented_requirements.requirement: Minimal UI displays the player's current HP and encountered monster stats
implemented_requirements.evidence: self.panel.config(text=... "HP: %d" and "Last monster:\n%s" showing the most recent monster name and HP

judge.summary: The provided code implements an 80x80 grid roguelike with W/A/S/D movement, wall collision, a door that advances levels, monsters that damage the player, treasure chests that heal 20‑30 HP, guaranteed maze connectivity, and a simple UI showing HP and last monster info. All core requirements are met and the program appears ready to run with Tkinter.
